sentences.text: Phasmagyps is an extinct genus of New World vulture from the family Cathartidae known from a single Oligocene fossil found in Colorado.
The genus contains one described species, Phasmagyps patritus, which is possibly the oldest known New World vulture.
When first described, Phasmagyps was estimated to be one-third larger than the modern Black vulture.
The preserved fossil has a largest diameter of 17.9 mm around the outer condyle and a width of 14.9 mm across the condyles.
The type specimen of Phasmagyps is a single fragmentary fossil bone housed in the Colorado Museum of Natural History with catalog number 1078.
The fossil was collected in 1923 by Philip Reinheinter from the Weld County Trigonias quarry.
Phasmagyps is classified within the subfamily Vulturinae.
Phasmagyps belongs to the family Cathartidae.
Phasmagyps lived during the Priabonian stage, approximately 37 to 33.9 million years ago.
The placement of Phasmagyps within the family Cathartidae has been questioned by researchers.
In 2005, Marcelo Stucchi and Steven Emslie maintained the placement of Phasmagyps in Cathartidae and noted it as the oldest member of the family in the Americas.
James Ducey's 1992 paper contradicts the original size estimate, stating Phasmagyps was not much larger than the Black Vulture.
